issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a function named create_zero_state(num_qubits) for the tensor-network part, but the template provides a function named init_zero_state(num_qubits) instead. The template's top-level docstring lists create_zero_state (matching the specification), yet the actual stub uses the different name init_zero_state. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the problem statement (or the provided tests) will look for create_zero_state and will not find it in the template, causing confusion or test failures.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the template stub init_zero_state to create_zero_state and keep the same signature (num_qubits: int -> list[NDArray[np.complex128]]). Alternatively, add a small wrapper create_zero_state that calls init_zero_state, so the template matches the function name and signature described by the problem statement and used in the solution/tests.

issues.description: The tensor-network zero-state constructor is named inconsistently across artifacts: the Problem Statement and Solution expect/create a function called create_zero_state(...), but the Template Repository provides a function named init_zero_state(...). This is the primary entry-point for creating the MPS zero state and is referenced in the task list and documentation, so the differing identifier will create a direct mapping confusion for students (they will look for create_zero_state as specified in the problem/tests but only find init_zero_state in the starter code).
issues.suggested_fix: Align the template function name with the problem statement and solution. Rename init_zero_state to create_zero_state in template_repository/tensor_networks.py (or provide a compatibility wrapper: define create_zero_state(...) that calls init_zero_state(...)). Update any in-file references and the docstring to consistently use create_zero_state so students can directly map the task description to the starter code and tests.
